articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris for January 2000 outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's upcoming activities, including star parties, observational astronomy classes, and general meetings with guest speakers for January and February. Additionally, the publication features an account by Jane Houston detailing her participation in the 1999 Leonid MAC Mission, where she helped measure meteor flux from aboard a research aircraft.

articles.title: Leonids Zenith Hourly Rate
articles.summary: This article details an airborne observation campaign for the 1999 Leonid meteor storm, conducted over several nights using various specialized cameras on an ARIA aircraft. The observations captured a peak Zenith Hourly Rate (ZHR) of 2300 Leonids per hour, with the author personally observing 2700, along with phenomena like sprites and meteors streaking through the Aurora Borealis. The report describes the observation techniques, equipment, and significant events from each night, culminating in a reflection on the successful scientific endeavor.

articles.title: Mercury Transit Report
articles.summary: Akkana Peck recounts observing a Mercury transit from Henry Coe State Park, San Jose, CA, despite initial forecasts of poor weather. The event, observed with various filtered telescopes, was surprisingly easier to see than predicted, allowing for clear views of sunspots and Mercury's contacts. The author critically examines the "black drop" effect, suggesting its manifestation might be influenced by atmospheric seeing conditions.

articles.title: Astronomy Educator Position Available
articles.summary: The Astronomical Society of the Pacific is seeking a full-time Astronomy Educator to develop K-12 and family-focused educational programs, create hands-on activities, and assist with grant writing and public outreach. The article also provides a detailed January 2000 observing report for planets like Jupiter and Saturn, along with a schedule of upcoming school star parties.

articles.title: Comet Comments for January 2000
articles.summary: This January 2000 'Comet Comments' column discusses the current status of Periodic Comet Machholz 2, noting it's fainter than expected but may be glimpsed, and details its next good visibility in 2015. It also mentions recent comet discoveries by the Catalina Sky Survey and analysis of SOHO satellite data. The article reflects on the future of visual comet hunting, acknowledging increased competition from automated surveys but suggesting amateurs can still find comets, albeit at a reduced rate, especially in areas near the sun.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar January 2000
articles.summary: This document outlines the "Celestial Calendar" for January 2000, providing comprehensive astronomical data for observers. It details lunar phases, planetary ephemerides (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) including their rise, transit, and set times, along with celestial coordinates. The calendar also includes information on the Sun's position, hours of darkness, astronomical twilight, and sidereal time for optimal skygazing.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope Status document provides an update on the availability of telescopes through the San Jose Astronomical Association's loaner program. It details which scopes are immediately available, which are currently on loan with due dates, and those with extended loan periods, along with a waiting list for popular equipment. Members interested in borrowing a scope are directed to contact Mike Koop for arrangements and pick-up at SJAA events.
